stories.title: OpenAI Urges California to Toughen Its AI Safety Bill
stories.summary: OpenAI told California lawmakers to strengthen the state's pending AI safety bill. Engadget and TechCrunch both reported the call. The move comes as states write their own AI rules while Congress stays on the sidelines.
stories.whyItMatters: State AI rules often set the pattern other states copy. OpenAI's position could shape US AI regulation for years.

stories.title: Harvard's $699 Startup Bootcamp Uses AI Avatars of Its Instructors
stories.summary: Harvard now offers a $699 startup bootcamp that includes AI avatars of its own instructors, TechCrunch reports. The program blends live teaching with AI-generated stand-ins.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows a top university putting AI avatars into paid coursework, a sign generative AI is moving from chatbots into mainstream education products.
whatToWatch: How students and alumni react to the AI avatar format
Whether other universities copy the model
questions: How much of the course actually uses the avatars versus live instructors?

stories.title: Apple's iPhone Trade-In Program Accepts Older Models Than Expected
stories.summary: Engadget reports that the oldest iPhone model Apple still accepts for trade-in credit is older than most people would guess. The trade-in program lets customers put an old iPhone's value toward a new purchase.
stories.whyItMatters: Trade-in programs push Apple's upgrade cycle and recommerce business, which affects how often customers buy new iPhones.
questions: Will Apple's cutoff model change as older iPhones lose support?

stories.summary: TechCrunch reports that US battery startups are increasingly relying on defense-sector funding and contracts to stay afloat. This comes as commercial battery markets, including EVs, face tougher conditions and competition from Chinese manufacturers.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows defense spending becoming a key funding source for clean-energy hardware startups, reshaping how these companies build their business models.

stories.summary: Engadget examines Waymo's current Level 4 automation status and explains what separates it from full Level 5 self-driving. The piece breaks down the gap between today's robotaxis and true driverless capability in all conditions.
stories.whyItMatters: It clarifies what autonomous vehicle companies have actually achieved versus their marketing claims, which matters as robotaxi services expand into more cities.

stories.title: Wired Guide Spotlights Android's Work Profile Feature
stories.summary: Wired published a guide on setting up a separate work profile on Android phones. The feature splits work and personal apps and data on one device.
stories.whyItMatters: It reflects the ongoing push for bring-your-own-device security as companies try to protect work data on phones employees also use personally.

stories.title: Apple Cuts Hundreds of Jobs Across Siri and Vision Pro Teams
stories.summary: Apple reportedly laid off more than 200 employees from its Siri and Vision Pro software teams. Engadget, TechCrunch, and The Verge all reported the cuts.
stories.whyItMatters: The cuts suggest Apple is rethinking its investment in voice AI and mixed reality, two areas central to how it competes with rivals on AI and new hardware categories.

stories.whyItMatters: Claims of beating major labs at real research tasks, not just benchmarks, fuel the competition among AI companies to prove practical scientific value.

stories.title: Pixel 11 Pro XL Review: Better Cameras, Still an Iterative Upgrade

stories.whyItMatters: It points to a broader slowdown in smartphone innovation, making it harder for Google to stand out against Apple and Samsung on hardware alone.
questions: Will Google lean more on software and AI features to differentiate future Pixels?

stories.title: Review: A $520 HP OmniBook Shows Why RAM Beats Polish
stories.summary: The Verge reviewed a $520 HP OmniBook with 16GB of RAM and found it outperforms nicer, pricier laptops that ship with only 8GB. The review argues RAM matters more than build quality for everyday use.
stories.whyItMatters: It highlights how OEM spec choices, not just price or design, shape real-world laptop value as PC makers compete on both cost and performance.
whatToWatch: Whether other budget laptop makers raise base RAM to compete
questions: Will 8GB configurations disappear from mainstream laptop lineups?

sources.title: An okay laptop with 16GB of RAM is better than a nice laptop with 8GB, and this $520 HP OmniBook proves it
